transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Marin (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO, Hawthorne ML), Elliot Park (Eng Mgr), Samir Rao (Principal ML Eng)

Summary: Quick integration/discovery to understand Hawthorne's planned product flow, ask about SDKs/instrumentation (LangChain/LlamaIndex usage), gateway/proxy patterns, quotas/rate-limits, and observability hooks. Customer leaning towards Dedicated for predictable latency but needs clarity on VPC/KMS and SDK adaptors.

Topics: integration paths (hosted vs dedicated vs private), LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway vs direct calls, rate limiting & throttles, observability hooks/tracing, security (KMS, SOC2), next steps for benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: okay everybody hi thanks for taking the time, this is Lena from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account
[00:07] Maya: hey Lena, thanks; i'm Maya CTO at Hawthorne, with Elliot and Samir here
[00:11] Diego: hi all, Diego from Redwood infra, i'll be part of the tech deep dive and benchmarks
[00:16] Elliot: thanks, quick ask \u0014 we wanted to validate integration patterns with our existing vector store which uses LlamaIndex, and also whether LangChain flows are first-class
[00:27] Samir: and we have strict latency targets for our user queries, around 150ms p50 for short text completions \u0014 so curious about batching tradeoffs
[00:38] Lena: great, that helps \u0014 high level, Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private. for your latency concerns Dedicated is common, but hosted with dedicated tier can work too depending on throughput. Diego can walk kernels/latency tradeoffs
[00:52] Diego: yeah quick note, our runtime has continuous batching and prefix KV cache \u0014 for short sequences we try to avoid batching overhead. we also have per-route configs so you can route low-latency endpoints to smaller batch windows. sometimes the transcripts show us as 'Redwood Dedi-cay-ted' in logs but, haha, ignore that
[01:10] Maya: (laughs) okay. on integration \u0014 we use Python LlamaIndex wrappers and some LangChain agents in prod. is there an SDK or adapter we should use?
[01:22] Diego: we have official SDKs in python/node, and we maintain adapter examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. most customers either call Redwood via our SDK or put a gateway/proxy in front to handle auth/routing. we published a LangChain connector in our docs, it's not a drop-in perfect but it's maintained
[01:38] Samir: any examples for LlamaIndex? we currently use LlamaIndex's retriever interface to call outbound models \u0014 want to avoid reworking a lot of code
[01:48] Diego: yes, we have a short example in the repo: how to swap the llm client to Redwood's SDK and keep the LlamaIndex retriever. i'll share the link. typical change is 3-5 lines to swap client instantiation.
[01:58] Elliot: good. what about rate limits and quotas \u0014 our traffic spikes 5x during business hours, and we need graceful throttling and backpressure handling
[02:09] Lena: we expose per-api-key quotas and per-route rate limits. for Dedicated you can have higher soft limits and configurable burst. for hosted customers we also support token-level quotas and adaptive rate limits tied to plan. Diego \u0014 observability knobs?
[02:22] Diego: we provide request-level logs, token counts, latency histograms, plus tracing hooks (open-telemetry friendly). you can emit spans from your app and link them to Redwood request ids. also we emit per-model metrics to cloudwatch/prometheus endpoints for Dedicated/private
[02:41] Maya: do you support propagating trace ids through a gateway? we already have an API gateway that injects x-trace-id
[02:47] Diego: yes that's common \u0014 we accept custom headers and preserve trace ids. for private deployments the control plane can be configured to ingest traces into your observability stack. note that some headers are sanitized for security but x-trace-id passes through by default.
[02:59] Samir: security: we need to ensure KMS integration for encryption keys and audit logs for compliance. can Dedicated be VPC-isolated?
[03:09] Lena: Dedicated is VPC peering or private link depending on cloud. we also support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and can rotate keys on schedule. we have SOC 2 + ISO docs, happy to share security whitepaper
[03:22] Elliot: ok can you share the security questionnaire answer set? we'll need it for procurement
[03:26] Lena: yep i'll attach our security pack and the standard questionnaire answers.
[03:30] Maya: about gateway vs direct calls \u0014 our infra team prefers a proxy that does routing and simple caching. would you recommend putting Redwood behind our proxy or calling directly from services?
[03:41] Diego: both approaches work. proxy in front is useful for request normalization, auth, and to apply custom caching. direct calls reduce one hop and slightly lower tail latency. for Dedicated customers sometimes we recommend a lightweight sidecar per service for better telemetry, but proxy is fine
[03:55] Samir: you mentioned prefix/KV cache \u0014 does that persist across requests or is it ephemeral in GPU memory?
[04:03] Diego: KV cache is per-inference instance and can be warmed via cache priming. we also support a shared prefix cache for repeated system messages; persistence across restarts is limited on hosted but in Dedicated you can leverage a small redis-backed hot cache for cross-instance warm starts
[04:19] Elliot: interesting. for our use case we have ~200 req/s sustained with spikes to 1k req/s. what's the typical Dedicated pool sizing for that?
[04:29] Diego: rough guess depends on model and sequence length. if you're using a 13B quantized model and average seq length is 60 tokens, you might need 4-6 GPUs for steady 200 req/s with low p50; for spikes we'd configure burst capacity and autoscaling. we'll need sample payloads to right-size accurately
[04:46] Maya: okay we'll provide sample traces. about LangChain \u0014 do you support function/tool calling patterns and structured outputs?
[04:55] Lena: yes, streaming with tools and function calling is supported; we return structured JSON and also partial streams. LangChain connectors handle streaming in the usual way but some adapters are async; Diego can point to examples
[05:07] Diego: note on streaming \u0014 if you need strict ordering and low-latency, prefer direct sdk streaming. proxies can buffer which increases latency.
[05:18] Samir: what about cost controls \u0014 can we cap token spend per route?
[05:23] Lena: yes, we have per-route budgets and token caps. alerting on spend is available in the console and via webhooks. for Dedicated we can set hard caps at the tenant level too.
[05:34] Elliot: good. another concern: we use LlamaIndex with local vector store, but some of our customers want private deployments on-prem. is Redwood Private a viable on-prem path?
[05:44] Lena: yes Private supports on-prem air-gapped installs with a control plane that can be customer-run. that path includes KMS integrations and audit logs but usually requires an enterprise engagement.
[05:55] Maya: latency parity with Dedicated \u0014 do you see comparable behavior?
[06:00] Diego: yes, Private on-prem will be as fast or faster if co-located with your services, but you have to handle infra ops. Dedicated gives the best blend of maintenance offload and predictable performance.
[06:11] Elliot: procurement and timeline \u0014 roughly how long to get Dedicated up if we sign a reserved capacity?
[06:18] Lena: typically 2\u20134 weeks to provision and test, depending on networking (VPC peering, IP allowlists). initial pilot can be faster with hosted slots.
[06:27] Maya: pipeline question \u0014 we have an LLM orchestration layer that picks models; will Redwood model catalog integrate with model selection policies?
[06:37] Diego: you can pin model versions via rollout configs and do A/B by route, we also offer smart routing by policy (latency, cost) out of the box, so your orchestrator could call different endpoints or we can expose weighted routing config
[06:51] Samir: about throttling \u0014 if a downstream model goes into OOM and latency spikes, do you support automatic fallback to a cheaper model?
[06:59] Diego: yes fallback policies are supported; you can define secondary model variants and automatic circuit-breakers per route. we also emit alerts and will route to a compatible variant when thresholds exceed.
notes: Customer uses LlamaIndex + LangChain in prod
Prefers Dedicated for latency but evaluating Hosted pilot first
Wants security pack and procurement questionnaire
